public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Lambda, a Series E AI & Software company founded by Stephen and Michael Balaban, has raised $3.15B to date. The comparable universe for AI & Software frontier companies includes one public peer (Palantir) and eight private competitors, though a narrow peer set meeting stage, sector, and valuation-tier criteria proved insufficient for robust median-based triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology was the applicable approach, using total capital raised ($3.15B) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E progression. This method yielded an implied valuation of $4.4B. A peer-median analysis was not executable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation profiles; the broader AI & Software universe of 12 firms did not provide three or more filtered datapoints, making sector-wide medians unreliable given Lambda's frontier positioning.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $3.7B to $5.1B, centered on $4.4B, derived from a single methodological input. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.4x multiplier for this specific company and stage environment, and the absence of directly comparable late-stage AI firms with disclosed valuation metrics. Resolution of these uncertainties—via additional transaction data or refined peer filtration—would strengthen conviction in the range.
